text:
carol: Quick q — should the console suggest analytics presets based on route traffic patterns + quota tier? Thinking per-route default filters that bias toward high-latency endpoints or cost spikes. e.g. for a route with bursty p95 show a 'latency regressions' suggestion. Thoughts?

bharat: I like the idea but worried about noise. We shouldn't auto-add presets to people's saved views. Suggest instead as an unobtrusive suggestion panel.

alice: +1 to suggestion panel. Maybe a single collapsible row: 'Suggested for this route' with 1–3 high-signal presets, user can pin. keeps the UI clean.

dave: From infra side we need to define the signals: p50/p95/p99, error rate delta, cost per request, model mismatch rate (route model != observed top model). Can we compute these cheaply?

emily: We already sample telemetry for route explorer. Adding a periodic job (6h) to compute heuristics is doable. Need to estimate extra storage for deltas. I'll surface numbers.

bharat: Also consider customer tier logic: Dedicated customers probably care more about throughput/SLA metrics, hosted customers about cost and token-patterns. Suggestions should be tier-aware.

alice: UX note — show a small reason badge on each suggestion (e.g. 'p95 high', 'cost spike', 'model drift'). Clicking the badge expands the actual filter and preview. That helps trust.

deploy-bot: Feature flag 'route_suggestions_v1' rolled out to 10% of orgs in staging.

dave: API shape idea: GET /api/v1/console/routes/:id/suggestions returns an array of {id, title, filters, reason, confidence}. Quick example:
```
[
  {"id":"latency-preset","title":"Latency regressions","filters":"latency.p95>800","reason":"p95>800ms over 12h","confidence":0.87}
]
```
We should also include a telemetry sample link for the preview.

carol: Good next steps — emily to add job + rough cost estimate, dave to draft API contract, alice to wireframe the 'Suggested for this route' chip and badge copy. I'll sync with PM on prioritization.

alice: thanks — i'll sketch two small mock variants and drop in #design by EOD. :thumbsup:
